  • he exploit targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic signing system rather than a smart contract bug.
  • The latest incident marks Chainflip’s second major security breach in just over two months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chainflip lost nearly $4.86 million after an attacker drained its Ethereum vault.

he exploit targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic signing system rather than a smart contract bug.

The latest incident marks Chainflip’s second major security breach in just over two months.

Industry observers note that chainflip, a decentralized cross-chain swap protocol, has faced another security scare after nearly $4.86 million in crypto was drained from its Ethereum vault in a single transaction. The attacker moved the stolen funds through Tornado Cash within just nine minutes, forcing the protocol to halt deposits, withdrawals, and swaps.

While its team investigates how the funds were taken.

On-chain investigations by Bitquery show that the attacker targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic key system rather than exploiting a bug in its smart contracts.

It has been revealed that the attacker first obtained a valid Schnorr signature from the Ethereum Vault’s Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) aggregate key. This allowed the attacker to pass the vault’s normal signature checks.

Industry observers note that on November 21, 2026, a newly funded wallet (0x78fa) called the Vault.transferBatch function. The transaction passed verification and drained all the vault’s available funds in a single move.

In a recent development, the attacker then moved rapidly to hide the stolen funds. Within nine minutes, the exploiter swapped the 3,249,631.41 USDC and 758,141.33 USDT for 2,909 ETH (worth around $4.86 million), then sent it to Tornado Cash in 38 separate batches.

Industry observers note that chainflip has not yet confirmed the $4.86 million loss. Instead, the protocol said it was aware of a potential exploit affecting its vaults and moved into full safe mode as a precaution.

We’re aware of a potential exploit affecting Chainflip vaults.As a precaution, the protocol is being put into full safe mode. Deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quoting are disabled.We’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.

“Deposits, withdrawals, swaps, and quoting are disabled; we’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.”.

Recent findings suggest that this is Chainflip’s second major attack in just over two months. On September 12, 2026, the protocol lost $736,442 in a separate exploit targeting its TRON integration. That attack was caused by a software flaw in how Chainflip processed TRON transaction data, while the November 21 attack targeted its Ethereum Vault’s cryptographic signing key.

After the September attack, Chainflip paused TRON swaps and used its surplus reserves to fully reimburse affected liquidity providers in USDC.

The protocol has yet to confirm whether it will follow the same recovery plan for the latest $4.86 million loss.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it launched its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a new, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core. The new bike keeps much of the moto-inspired styling and performance of the existing Scrambler Hardtail, but trims back several components to knock several hundred dollars off the price.

The new Scrambler Core starts at $1,399, compared to $1,699 for the existing Scrambler Hardtail.

Juiced is also offering a $1,599 long-range version of the Core, as well as a smaller “Midsize” frame that should make the bike much more accessible to shorter riders – and, perhaps more importantly, teenagers.

Teens are a major part of the moto-style e-bike market, and Juiced has designed its Scrambler e-bikes as a safer option for those younger riders. In addition to ensuring street-legal performance for most major markets, Juiced rolled out a feature known as Speed Lock, which is essentially a parental control option that lets a parent or guardian set a lower speed limit using a PIN code that prevents their teen from later modifying the speed limit.

It has been revealed that the launch comes as part of the rebirth of Juiced Bikes following the brand’s acquisition last year. The company was founded in 2009 and was acquired in 2025 by the co-founders of Lectric Ebikes, who have since brought the brand back with a newly introduced generation of its popular Scrambler platform.

The biggest changes appear to be in the powertrain, battery, brakes, and suspension.

Industry observers note that the standard Scrambler Hardtail debuted earlier this year set the standard for the flagship models by using a 750W nominal motor with 90 Nm of torque and reaching 28 mph (45 km/h). Its 52V 19.2Ah battery provides nearly 1 kWh of capacity and a claimed range of up to 60 miles (96 km).

Recent findings suggest that the Scrambler Core steps down to a 500W nominal rear hub motor rated for 1,176W peak and 80 Nm of torque. Top speed is also reduced slightly to 25 mph (40 km/h), while the throttle is limited to 20 mph (32 km/h). Importantly, though, Juiced has retained its 52V architecture, meaning this is still a fairly punchy setup rather than a dramatically detuned budget bike.

Battery capacity takes a hit as well. The standard Core gets a 52V 10Ah battery with 520 Wh of capacity, rated for up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Spending another $200 gets the Core Long-Range with a 52V 15Ah, 780Wh battery and a claimed 60-mile (96 km) maximum range. As with nearly all e-bikes, expect real-world range to fall short of the idealized advertised numbers, which are generally only achievable under the lowest power pedal assist.

Juiced also traded the Talon P4 four-piston hydraulic brakes found on the more expensive Scrambler for Talon P2 two-piston brakes. The KKE inverted fork with 140mm of travel is gone too, replaced by a more conventional aluminum triple-crown fork with 100mm of travel.

Industry observers note that those are meaningful downgrades, but they’re also largely the kinds of changes I’d expect to see when trying to shave $300 off an already competitively priced moto-style e-bike. It’s a strategy we’ve seen play out before in the industry, helping lower costs for riders who want a flagship bike but don’t necessarily want to pay flagship prices.

Recent findings suggest that even so, notable features remain to help maintain the look and feel of the Juiced Scrambler line. The Core still gets 20 x 4-inch fat tires, hydraulic disc brakes, a frame-integrated TFT display, four pedal-assist levels, a headlight, taillight, brake light, and turn signals. It’s a single-speed setup and weighs 73 lb (33 kg), while being rated for a 300 lb (136 kg) payload.

Perhaps the more interesting addition is the Scrambler Core Midsize.

While the regular Core is recommended for riders 5’2” and taller, the Midsize drops that figure to just 4’10”. Pricing remains the same: $1,399 with the 520Wh battery or $1,599 with the 780Wh long-range pack.

And with an eye towards safety, the Core and Core Mini retain Juiced’s PIN-protected parental speed lock. Parents can set the motor-assisted top speed anywhere from 1-25 mph and lock the setting behind a four-digit PIN. That makes even more sense on the Midsize version, which seems tailor-made for younger riders who want the moto-style look but may not yet comfortably fit the larger Scrambler.

Recent findings suggest that the Core is launching in several decidedly Juiced color names, including Black Nectar, Fruit Punch, Sour Grape, White Grape, Berry Freeze, and Blood Orange, though availability varies between frame sizes and battery configurations. Juiced says preorders are expected to begin shipping around the end of the month.

Industry observers note that at $1,399, the Scrambler Core feels like a logical extension of Juiced’s rebooted lineup. You lose some battery, motor power, braking hardware, suspension travel, and a few mph compared to the Hardtail, but the underlying recipe is largely intact. For riders who mostly want the Scrambler look and feel – or parents shopping for a smaller rider – saving $300 may be a pretty compelling trade. Especially when you consider that the original Juiced Scrambler already led the industry in value for moto-style e-bikes from reputable brands.

Toss in the strong backing from Lectric and the 3-year warranty, and it’s hard to consider much else among the competition.

Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to problem loans and track repayments onchain.".

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool demonstrated the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

In a recent development, through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

In a recent development, the amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan notes on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting new safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.

The new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature. That location can then appear in real time to nearby drivers using Waze, with cyclists displayed as moving icons on the road.

As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.

I’ve long maintained that safety – or more accurately, the perception that cycling isn’t safe – is one of the biggest impediments to getting more people onto bikes.

It has been revealed that that’s especially true in the US, where cyclists are often forced to share roads with cars instead of enjoying the kind of widespread separated cycling infrastructure found in many more bike-friendly countries. And when a cyclist and a multi-ton vehicle have to occupy the same space, making sure the driver knows that cyclist is there can make a major difference.

According to recent reports, of course, an icon on Waze isn’t going to magically make cycling safe. It won’t replace protected bike lanes, better road design, slower vehicle speeds, or attentive drivers.

But I can certainly imagine situations where it could help. Riding at night or in poor visibility, approaching a blind curve, or simply traveling on a narrow road where a driver might otherwise come upon a cyclist unexpectedly are all situations where an advance warning could be useful.

Sources indicate that the feature is opt-in through Garmin Connect and activates when the cyclist starts an outdoor cycling activity. Garmin notes location sharing is temporary and session-based, and that cyclists’ personal information isn’t displayed in Waze. Of course, anyone who uses a personal GPS device has already accepted that their location is shared with Significant Tech in exchange for features they value, but at least we know that any personalized info stays within Garmin instead of proliferating even further.

This is cool but requires both a Garmin product and the Waze app. IMHO better to equip fresh cars and trucks with bicycle and pedestrian detection.

According to recent reports, garmin LiveTrack itself is free for people with compatible Garmin devices and previously allowed cyclists to share their live location, speed, route, and other information with friends and family. I’ve used it myself as a safety feature when venturing off-road and on longer solo journeys. The Waze integration essentially expands that safety net to nearby motorists.

There’s obviously one significant limitation: You need to be riding with a compatible Garmin device, and the driver needs to be using Waze.

But with Waze claiming around 200 million users globally and Garmin being one of the biggest names in cycling computers and fitness watches, that’s not exactly a tiny Venn diagram.

Anything that gives drivers another chance to see cyclists before actually seeing them sounds like a win to me.

  • BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the newly introduced i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.

BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

Industry observers note that the Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

BMW drove the latest i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.

The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse.

BMW said the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.

The latest i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.

BMW stated the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

The vehicle was driven at all times by a single driver and was not modified in any way, in terms of hardware or software, from the standard i3 available for purchase.

BMW’s newly introduced i3 uses a 108.7 kWh battery and Gen6 eDrive system that provides a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

With a drag coefficient of just 0.21, the newly introduced i3 is the most aerodynamically efficient BMW vehicle to date.

In the US, BMW remarked the newly introduced 2027 i3 50 xDrive will offer an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 468 miles.

Recent findings suggest that with an 800V architecture, the electric sedan can add nearly 262 miles (423 km) of range (WLTP) in about 10 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds up to 400 kW. In the US, the i3 has a built-in NACS port.

According to recent reports, very reasonable. I've been with NK iX3 from Spain to Estonia and the experience is real - low consumption, great comfort and really fast charging. And there are more and more high speed chargers every month.

Like the fresh iX3, the i3 features BMW’s Neue Klasse interior design. The setup consists of BMW’s massive 43″ Panoramic Vision display that spans the base of the windshield and a 17.9″ floating central infotainment display.

The latest BMW i3 50 xDrive is on sale in Germany starting at €65,900 with a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

In the US, the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive and 2027 iX3 50 xDrive are available to order, both starting at $61,500.

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

Recent findings suggest that TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG organization that builds on Bittensor.

According to recent reports, at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert said that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson mentioned.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

The November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

Recent findings suggest that TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Recent findings suggest that shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

It has been revealed that A GREAT UNDERSHIRT is my first line of defense against sweat, stains, and overheating. It’s like the menswear equivalent of SPF. I learned that the hard way years ago, when I wore a flimsy cotton tee under a light-blue dress shirt to a summer wedding and, by cocktail hour, looked like I’d run a 10K instead of walked down the aisle. Never again. Now, if I’m layering under a dress shirt or sweater, I want something that works hard without me ever thinking about it. The best undershirts are so comfortable, I forget they’re even on. Unlike cheap, bulky options that ride up, trap heat, or lose their shape after a few washes, the real standouts are lightweight, moisture-wicking, and cut with a trim fit that stays put without squeezing the life out of you. They also tuck away neatly into trousers and save your other shirts from pit stains.

To find the GOATs, our fashion team and I tested more than 50 styles—everything from V-neck tees and tank tops to classic white crewnecks—wearing them under button-downs, sweaters, and even on their own. The winners disappear under your clothes like a good stunt double, regulate temperature like built-in AC, and keep you looking cool, calm, and collected from your morning commute to last call.

Hanes is perhaps the most famous undershirt brand on the planet. I’ve been wearing its undergarments since I was about 10 years old, and over the time, they've just become better in terms of fit and feel. For example, I’ve been wearing Hanes’ performance undershirt for four months, and it’s consistently comfortable, breathable, and snug in all the right places.

Sources indicate that the shoulders sit perfectly without pulling, the chest drapes close without clinging, and the sleeves are tailored to follow your arms without cutting into your biceps. When an undershirt feels this light, I brace myself for it to be flimsy and tear like tissue, but it's impressively solid—and I didn’t even sweat in it. Unlike other undershirts that I’ve tested, this one has a structured collar and hem that keeps its shape. The polyester-rayon fabric is extra smooth and cool to the touch, even after wearing it for hours at the office. I also appreciate that the fabric blend is much lighter in weight than a traditional cotton undershirt.

After putting it through at least eight washes, I noticed that the fabric didn’t fade or shrink. One way I preserve it is by letting it air dry instead of tossing it in the dryer under high heat. It’s long enough to tuck in and doesn’t bunch under an overshirt. Since it's blended with a hint of stretch, I could grab a box off a high shelf without any restriction. Hanes uses the same double-needle stitching to reinforce the neck, sleeves, and hem as with their regular undershirts. This will stand up to years of washing and wearing with steady use. It only comes in white, but you can wear it with so many different fits—solo or layered.

It has been revealed that undershirts come in three main styles—crewneck, V-neck, and tank tops (A-shirts)—each designed for different layering needs, body types, and personal preferences. Choosing the right one can affect everything from comfort and breathability to how well your outer layers look.

Recent findings suggest that the classic undershirt style features a round neckline that sits at the base of the neck. This is best for guys who want to fully cover their chest, while blending under crewneck sweaters, sweatshirts, and casual shirts. This also prevents chest hair from showing through thin shirts.

Recent findings suggest that an undershirt with a V-shaped neckline, designed to stay hidden under an unbuttoned shirt or deeper-cut sweaters. It’s perfect for those who want a low-profile look and prefer to leave the top button of their dress shirt undone, so it’s almost invisible unlike crewnecks. V-Neck undershirts allow more breathability at the neck, especially in warmer weather.

On the other hand, we have tank tops—a sleeveless undershirt with wide shoulder straps and a scooped neckline. This style is often cut the lowest, to the chest, and reveals the least under another cloth or on its own. It’s perfect for guys who want less bulk, more arm mobility and extra breathability in hot weather.

Undershirts come in a range of fits, each with different benefits depending on personal preference and outfit choice.

In a recent development, this fit is close to the body, but not skin-tight. It’s a go-to option if you like a clean, tailored look, making it ideal for layering under dress shirts since it won’t bunch up.

This fit is tighter than slim fit but still comfortable. It works well under fitted clothing but doesn’t feel restrictive. Cotton-blend undershirts with a little stretch (spandex or elastane) excel here.

Looser and more breathable, offering more movement than slim or snug fits. Works well for casual outfits but can bunch up under fitted dress shirts.

The least restrictive, but can feel bulky under layers. On the flip side, it's great for lounging or wearing on its own.

Since 2021, I’ve worked alongside our fashion team—led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan—to test more than 50 undershirts at the office, beneath sweaters on chilly nights, layered under jackets, or even rocking them solo in the spring-summer months. We graded each undershirt on style, comfort, price, versatility, and overall performance. That meant paying close attention to moisture-wicking ability, stretch and recovery, breathability, and durability. To make sure our picks worked beyond our own closets, we also gathered feedback from testers across different body types and fit preferences. We also conferred with menswear expert Ted Stafford, who's spent decades evaluating everything from tailoring to boots. His expertise, along with our in-the-field testing, helped us lock in the 16 best undershirts for men that actually live up to the hype.

While most undershirts for men are designed to be thin and worn as a base layer beneath other garments, they can also be worn alone as just a T-shirt or a tank top in certain situations. For instance, a high-quality, well-fitted undershirt can be worn on its own during hot summer days or as part of a casual loungewear outfit. In fact, undershirts with breathability and moisture-wicking properties are perfect as standalone shirts as well. These undershirts often have a slightly thicker fabric, additional detailing (like a pocket), or a more fashionable cut to ensure a polished look that doesn't make you look like you're just wearing a tried-and-true undershirt.

Wearing an undershirt is a wise choice for men seeking both style and practicality. The best undershirts for men will help absorb sweat and prevent it from seeping into your outer garments as sweat marks, keeping you fresh and dry throughout the day. Hence, for men who are prone to sweat, undershirts will really extend the lifespan of your outer garments by acting as an additional layer of protection between them and your body. For men who run hot, undershirts made from breathable materials will also keep you cool by wicking away moisture. The best undershirts will also help enhance comfort by acting as a barrier between your skin and the rough texture of certain fabrics (like itchy wool), reducing irritation and preventing your outer shirt from clinging to your body. During colder seasons, an undershirt also adds an extra layer of warmth.

The number of undershirts a man should own depends on his personal preference and lifestyle. However, as a general rule of thumb, it's recommended to have a rotation of at least 5 to 7 undershirts to ensure that you have a fresh one for each day of the week. This gives each undershirt ample time to rest and recover between wears and allows for regular washing, ensuring that you always have a fresh undershirt ready. This rotation not only helps prolong their lifespan but also makes sure each undershirt is not subjected to excessive wear and tear.

Tech Report: BYD and Geely approached FIA about a 12th F1 team, indicates Ben Sulayem

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1030 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed.
  • It has been revealed that but there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither tech giant has a deal.
  • “One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem mentioned of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem named the two Chinese automakers while speaking at the New Economy Forum in Madrid, as first reported by Grande Prêmio.

It has been revealed that but there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither tech giant has a deal. The FIA is also pushing F1 toward the kind of engine an EV maker has the least reason to build.

“One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem mentioned of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.

He remarked he suggested that BYD buy an existing team instead of starting a upcoming one. BYD wasn’t interested in that route. It wants its own team, so Ben Sulayem told the company to come back with a “serious proposal” that shows the project can work.

Industry observers note that he also made it clear that Chinese manufacturers won’t get special treatment. Any bid would go through the same process as other prospective entrants, and the rules won’t be rewritten to suit them. Right now, there’s no expansion process at all: the FIA isn’t actively looking for a 12th team.

Still, Ben Sulayem repeated that he’d like F1’s next newcomer to come from China, pointing to the country’s EV technology and the Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai.

In a recent development, this isn’t fresh for BYD. Back in March, we reported that BYD was exploring a Formula 1 entry, either by buying a team or building one from scratch.

In April, executive vice president Stella Li noted BYD had met F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali in Shanghai and that an entry was “something we’re discussing.” By July, the tone had cooled. Li said “the dream is always there, but we don’t have a concrete agenda,” and special advisor Alfredo Altavilla set a clear condition: “We will never participate in Formula 1 just to put a sticker on the side of a car.”.

Altavilla remarked BYD would only consider F1 to the extent its technology can serve the sport.

Geely is the newly introduced name here. The group sold 3.02 million vehicles last year and owns Volvo, Polestar, and Lotus, a brand with decades of F1 history. It’s also heading into Canada next year as Chinese automakers push hard into new markets.

The last newcomer, Cadillac, took a long road. The FIA opened an expression-of-interest process in 2023, and GM’s team only joined the grid as the 11th team this season, running Ferrari power until its own power unit arrives. Audi got in the other way, by taking over Sauber.

Here’s where it gets awkward for an EV maker. The 2026 F1 power units split output roughly 50/50 between the combustion engine and electric power, with the MGU-K jumping to 350 kW.

The FIA is already walking that back. In June, it agreed to shift the split to 60-40 in favor of combustion for 2027 and 2028. And Ben Sulayem has been pushing for V8 engines running on sustainable fuel with “minor electrification” for the next rules cycle, starting in 2031 at the latest, possibly 2030. Domenicali notes F1 should have a package ready to discuss by the end of this year.

So the FIA president wants a Chinese EV maker on the grid, while pushing a rulebook that makes their main strength less relevant.

We like the idea of BYD or Geely in F1. Chinese automakers have the money and the engineers, and they badly need brand prestige outside China. BYD in particular has been on a performance push with Yangwang, and F1 would be the loudest possible way to tell Europe it’s not just a cheap car brand.

It has been revealed that they look for visibility/recognition on the world stage, regardless EVs. And in some (primitive) markets they market themselves as hybrids automakers, not as EV automakers.

They will make a hybrid power unit (which they already make anyway) to comply with the backward F1 regulations.

According to recent reports, but Ben Sulayem’s comments don’t move things much. There’s no entry process, BYD has already turned down his main suggestion, and Geely’s interest is a name dropped at a conference, not a bid.

Industry observers note that A Chinese would likely be good for F1 as well. Motorsports are on the rise in China, and that would be the cherry on top in helping popularize the sport in the world’s largest market.

The bigger glitch is the engine. Altavilla was clear that BYD isn’t interested in slapping a logo on a car. It wants F1 to showcase its technology, and BYD’s technology is batteries and electric drive. The FIA’s V8 push goes the other way. It’s hard to sell an EV giant on a sport that’s reducing the electric part of the powertrain.

  • According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is at the moment facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further shows that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is important to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

According to recent reports, at the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data demonstrates that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, is flashing a major, ‘scary’ technical signal that was absent even during its last major crashes in February and June 2026.

The flagship coin has crashed to a fresh 4.5-month low amid persistent institutional outflows totaling billions from cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

$BTC hasn't formed a higher high for 16 consecutive days now. This didn't even happen during the Feb 2026 and June 2026 crashes. https://t.co/I6IPmdueEc.

According to recent reports, bitcoin has failed to form a higher high for the past 16 days. This is a very long stretch, one that was absent during Bitcoin’s February and June crashes.

A higher high, in the context of technical analysis, is formed when an asset’s price reaches a fresh high point above its previous swing high. The absence of higher highs signals that buyers are having a hard time taking back control of the market.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

Earlier today, BTC crashed to $61,225, its lowest price point in around four and a half months.

Bitcoin's failure to create higher highs despite several attempts to recover indicates that selling pressure remains quite high.

Nevertheless, this technical pattern of 16 days without a higher high does not necessarily spell more pain for Bitcoin. If the cryptocurrency can decisively push above recent resistance zones, it may be a sign that buyers are starting to make a comeback.

Bitcoin is facing persistent withdrawals of huge amounts of money from U.S.-based spot Bitcoin ETFs.

In a recent development, blackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) witnessed its biggest-ever daily net outflow on Nov. 19.

In a recent development, the crypto fund suffered a whopping $541.1 million in net withdrawals on the day. At the same time, total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs amounted to around $582.3 million across the entire market.

In a recent development, more alarmingly, the fresh wave of withdrawals brings cumulative net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs to around $3.47 billion so far this November.

The ETFs have seen negative net flows on 12 of the first 14 trading days of the month.

  • After unveiling the Yangwang Altior in the UAE on Monday, its newly introduced ultra-luxury flagship electric sedan, BYD showcased its latest breakthrough technology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s Flash Charging tech can charge an EV in as little as five minutes. Now, BYD is taking things a step further with integrated solar power and a robotic arm that plugs itself in. See how it all works in action.

After unveiling the Yangwang Altior in the UAE on Monday, its newly introduced ultra-luxury flagship electric sedan, BYD showcased its latest breakthrough technology.

The Chinese automaker rolled out a new integrated charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that brings BYD’s “Three Green Dreams” to life.

In 2006, BYD president and CEO Wang Chuanfu revealed his vision of “Three Green Dreams,” including harnessing solar power to generate renewable energy, storing that energy in batteries, and replacing gas-powered vehicles with electric ones that run on clean energy.

The new charging system is the “world’s first,” according to BYD, to integrate solar power generation, energy storage, Flash Charging, and robotic charging together in one solution.

Industry observers note that BYD’s Flash Charging tech enables a vehicle’s battery to charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes, essentially the same time it takes to fill up at a gas station. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

The new robotic charging arm automatically locates the vehicle’s charging port, opens its cover, plugs in, and then removes it once the session is over.

By combining robotic charging with its Automated Valet Parking, BYD said the newly introduced tech goes beyond automated driving and parking to the charging process itself.

Once the vehicle is parked, the robotic charging arm automatically takes over and connects it to Flash Charging without the driver even touching the cable.

A post shared by Michael Martinez (@mmichael_martinez).

Michaël Martinez, head of marketing at BYD France, posted a video (shown above) showcasing the new charging tech in action.

The integrated solution is built around BYD’s Solar-Storage-Charging (SSC) system, fusing solar energy generation, battery storage, and its 5-minute Flash Charging tech. Together, the setup captures energy from the sun, stores it, and distributes it as needed.

If they could tie this into a smart summon type of capability, where the vehicle communicates with the charger and moves the vehicle into the proper location for charging and then moves to a parking spot once charging is complete. Rental car fleets would benefit and so would those in shopping centers. There are so many possibilities and this looks far more mature that the old snake charging Tesla demoed.

BYD has over 16 years of experience in the solar industry with a portfolio that includes solar cells, modules, and systems.

Its solar division, BYD Solar, does business in over 100 countries and regions. By using solar power, BYD said, the SCC system can operate independently off-the-grid.

The new technology is part of BYD’s wider Flash Charging rollout. By the end of 2027, the company aims to deploy 6,000 Flash Charging stations globally.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being launched in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

Sources indicate that these numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

Recent findings suggest that this, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

Industry observers note that latest EV prices edged up in October, but buyers still paid less than they did a year ago. The average transaction price for a new EV in the US was $56,220, up 1% from September and down 2.7% from October 2025, according to Kelley Blue Book, a Cox Automotive brand.

Across all new vehicles, the average hit a record $51,109, up 1.3% from September and 2.1% year over year, even as prices rose more slowly than they typically do in October.

It has been revealed that EV incentives barely budged from September’s revised 11.2% of the average transaction price to 11.3% in October. That’s up from 10.3% a year earlier and well above October’s industrywide average of 6.8%.

Tesla’s average selling price fell from September to $54,194, but it was still up 1.2% year over year. The Cybertruck helped push that average higher. Cox Automotive estimates Tesla sold 1,914 Cybertrucks in October, its best month in more than a year, at an average price of $92,380.

Sources indicate that the sad thing is that there likely is a market for an affordable electric pickup truck in the U.S. to compete with Ford’s F150 and others. The Ford Fathom may be the best fit for that market, now.

That sales bump comes as Tesla prepares to end Cybertruck production at its Austin factory in mid-2027. Elon Musk said Tesla will dismantle the assembly line around June or July to make room for more Cybercab robotaxis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into upcoming industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop newly introduced services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

Recent findings suggest that in 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each firm can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Sources indicate that trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

According to recent reports, whiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for customers in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The company also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

Recent findings suggest that WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into upcoming products and services.

In a recent development, “Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million owners. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making new technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” remarked Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

Breaking: Lucid CEO admits it ‘did not even know where cars were’ and lost orders

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lucid (LCID) CEO Silvio Napoli admitted on the firm’s Q3 earnings call that, as recently as this summer, the automaker “did not even know where cars were.” Buyers placed orders, Lucid took up to two weeks to locate and deliver a car, and some of those buyers walked away.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s a rough admission from a company sitting on thousands of unsold vehicles.
  • Recent findings suggest that napoli made the comment when an analyst asked whether Lucid’s deliveries would go up or down in the fourth quarter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lucid (LCID) CEO Silvio Napoli admitted on the firm’s Q3 earnings call that, as recently as this summer, the automaker “did not even know where cars were.” Buyers placed orders, Lucid took up to two weeks to locate and deliver a car, and some of those buyers walked away.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a rough admission from a company sitting on thousands of unsold vehicles. And it’s a problem Tesla ran into, and fixed, back in 2018 at more than ten times Lucid’s current volume.

Recent findings suggest that napoli made the comment when an analyst asked whether Lucid’s deliveries would go up or down in the fourth quarter. He said that at the start of Q3, the company had orders where it “would take sometimes two weeks to deliver to the customer, and so we would lose the order.”.

He remarked Lucid now has visibility on which cars are being built, where they’re shipped, where they’re stored, and when they can reach a customer. A fresh commercial team also now sells the cars it knows are available on the day a customer wants one.

According to recent reports, lucid built 3,228 more vehicles than it delivered in the first half of 2026, including 5,500 built but only 3,093 delivered in Q1. Its inventory hit $1.38 billion on the balance sheet at the end of June, which is why we reported earlier this year that Lucid had to adjust production after a bloated Q1 inventory.

So Lucid had thousands of cars on lots and in transit, and it was still losing buyers because it couldn’t match a car to an order fast enough.

In Q3, Lucid cut production to 2,954 vehicles and delivered 3,806, down 7% year over year. Finished goods inventory fell by almost 15% during the quarter, according to new CFO Alexander De Bock. Inventory stood at $1.22 billion on September 30.

Tesla learned this lesson the hard way during the Model 3 ramp.

Industry observers note that by Q3 2018, Tesla was making roughly 4,000 Model 3s per week. That’s more cars every week than Lucid delivers in a full quarter today. Deliveries tripled or quadrupled in some markets, and the bottleneck moved from the factory to the trucks.

Industry observers note that elon Musk tweeted in September 2018 that Tesla had “gone from production hell to delivery logistics hell.” A week later, he mentioned Tesla was facing an “extreme shortage of car carrier trailers” and had started building its own car carriers to keep cars moving. Tesla also released door-to-door delivery and asked existing owners to help at delivery centers.

It didn’t stop there. In November 2018, with the federal tax credit about to be cut in half for Tesla buyers, Musk said Tesla had bought trucking companies and locked in contracts with major haulers. Tesla moved cars east by truck instead of rail to cut weeks off transit times.

Tesla delivered 83,500 vehicles in Q3 2018, including 55,840 Model 3s, a record at the time.

When Model 3 reached Europe in February 2019, the first ship docked at Zeebrugge in Belgium and Tesla immediately had trouble processing the cars at the port.

In a recent development, about a week after the first ship arrived, Tesla ended its contract with the company preparing Model 3s at the port and took over the work itself. The target was 3,000 cars per week coming through one port.

Industry observers note that it worked. By March 2019, Tesla delivered more than 5,300 Model 3s in Norway alone, making it the best-selling car in the country by a wide margin. A car that’s sitting at a port or on a lot doesn’t make anyone money. Tesla treated delivery speed as a sales tool, not a back-office job.

We later learned from Musk himself that this “logistic hell” was almost the nail in Tesla’s coffin. The CEO remarked that Tesla was at the brink of bankruptcy at the time.

I like to think people were relatively patient with Tesla's growing pains when Model 3 was ramping up in 2018, largely because there weren't many alternatives for a sporty, relatively affordable EV.

But it's 2026. Buyers have plenty of options now, and the patience that early EV adopters once had for these kinds of mistakes is long gone.

This is one of the most embarrassing admissions we’ve heard on an earnings call, and credit to Napoli for saying it out loud. Most executives would have blamed “demand” and moved on.

It has been revealed that but it explains a lot. Lucid’s problem has never been the cars. The Air and Gravity are excellent products. The problem has been everything around them: service, software, and now we learn, basic inventory tracking. When you’re spending about $273,000 for every car you deliver, losing a buyer because you can’t find their car two weeks after they ordered is brutal.

Tesla solved this at 4,000 Model 3s a week while fighting for its own survival. Lucid is moving fewer than 300 cars a week. This isn’t a hard problem at that scale. It’s a discipline problem, and Napoli is right to call it that.

NEAR Protocol (NEAR) fell 11.41% on Nov. 20 and traded at $2.84, according to TradingView data. In early October, the token was trading near $6, and it has lost about half of its value since then.

Over the same period, the volume of NEAR Intents went up. "NEAR went from $6 to $3 in about a month. funny thing is, NEAR Intents is doing more volume now than it did in october," NEAR ecosystem contributor Evgeny Haenko wrote on X on Nov. 20.

Recent findings suggest that according to Haenko, NEAR Intents averaged around $129 million in daily volume in October, and in November it was processing around $134 million a day. "The price got cut in half, the business didn't slow down at all. hard for me to be bearish here," he wrote.

According to recent reports, NEAR Intents lets customers swap assets across more than 30 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP. The service is built into wallets such as Ledger, Trust Wallet and Brave. Over the past year, its trading volume grew 7.1 times to $39.5 billion.

Sources indicate that NEAR Intents has collected about $63 million in fees in total, and the network keeps about 29% of that amount. Fees on the NEAR Intents interface, payments from B2B partners and the spread on better-than-market trades accounted for 16.3%, 9.9% and 2.8% of the fees, respectively. Over the last 30 days, the protocol earned about $1.8 million, compared with $2.2 million in October.

Since February 2026, the protocol has used NEAR Intents revenue to buy NEAR on the market. More than 1.84 million NEAR have gone to the buyback wallet so far, and that is 41.6% of all distributed onchain revenue. Base transaction fees on the network are burned in full.

In early November, the NEAR community also voted to cut the maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over two years. The proposal, HSP-029, went through House of Stake, NEAR's governance initiative, and Haenko is one of its participants.

On Sept. 29, Bitwise debuted the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF on NYSE Arca under the ticker NRR. Two days later, on Oct. 1, NEAR Intents paused its services after an exploit that cost about $3.8 million, and the team promised to compensate users in full. The exploiter later returned the funds. "The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents hack were sent back in full," NEAR Intents general manager Alex Shevchenko remarked at the time.

Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
  • According to recent reports, A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) said in a report published on Thursday.
  • "Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.

According to recent reports, A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) said in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said in a statement.

The 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.

It has been revealed that IOSCO said the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day.".

Swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report noted. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.

Because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO remarked. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.

Wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has stated. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.

According to recent reports, the report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.

Layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report remarked.

Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.

Recent findings suggest that IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to enhancement cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.

Most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.

According to recent reports, no surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO stated it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.

According to recent reports, quantum hardware is advancing quickly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has mentioned it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

It has been revealed that on 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and Latest York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

Sources indicate that however, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

It has been revealed that for the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Industry observers note that is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

  • So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia opened orders for two new PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK.

In a recent development, the PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business. Built on Hyundai Motor’s dedicated modular skateboard platform, E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to enable “limitless possibilities.”.

So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.

According to recent reports, kia added the PV5 Chassis, an open-bed model that can be converted into just about anything. In the UK, Kia is offering conversions through TGS Automotive Group, including lightweight tipper, Dropside, and Box solutions.

The PV5 Chassis is available exclusively with the long-range 71.2 kWh battery in the UK, which Kia said could offer a potential WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km).

For reference, the PV5 Cargo L2/H1, which uses the same 71.2 kWh battery, offers a WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km). Other markets will also have a standard-range 51.1 kWh option.

The Chassis model is 4,610 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,935 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

Its compact size and 5.5-meter turning radius, Kia mentioned, make it easy to maneuver in city streets, construction sites, and other tight work areas.

Inside, the PV5 Chassis features two seats. Like other variants, it includes a 12.9″ navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display with standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Sources indicate that the Chassis model supports DC fast charging up to 120 kW, enabling the battery to charge from 10% to 80% in about 30 minutes. Using an 11 kW AC supply, it takes about 6 hours and 30 minutes to charge from 10% to 100%.

In a recent development, payload depends on the configuration. Kia mentioned the Dropside offers a payload of up to 633 kg, while the Tipper can carry 561 kg.

In the UK, the PV5 Chassis is now on sale from £32,916 ($43,400) on the road, including the expected £5,000 ($6,700) UK Zero Emission Van Grant.

Recent findings suggest that however, it’s an “incomplete vehicle,” as Kia describes it. The converted PV5 Dropside is priced from £40,110 ($53,500) on the road, including the ZEVG, while the PV5 Tipper starts at £41,310 ($55,000).

Kia also launched the larger PV5 Cargo L2/H2 in the UK. The new variant is 4,695mm long, 1,895mm wide, and 2,200mm high, with a 2,995mm wheelbase.

The taller roof opens up an internal cargo-area height of 1,815mm. It also offers a greater load capacity than the L1/H1 and L2/H2, with 5.2 cubic meters.

It’s available in three- and four-door configurations with the choice of two or three seats. The three-door versions have a maximum payload of 630 kg, while the four-door models have dual sliding doors and offer a payload of up to 600 kg. Both versions can tow up to 1,500 kg.

Like the Chassis model, the PV5 Cargo L2/H2 is available in the UK exclusively with the 71.2 kWh battery, which provides a WLTP range of up to 239 miles.

Inside, it features the same setup as the other PV5 variants, including a 12.9″ touchscreen navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display.

The base PV5 Cargo L2/H2 Essential two-seat starts at £35,016 ($46,700), on the road, including ZEVG.

Industry News: Tesla tuner Unplugged offers to take over Cybertruck production

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1174 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive.
  • It comes just four days after Elon Musk mentioned Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.
  • UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The tech giant says it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive. The firm publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors.

It comes just four days after Elon Musk mentioned Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.

UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The tech giant says it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”.

Industry observers note that in exchange, Tesla would collect a license fee plus FSD and Robotaxi network revenue on every vehicle built. UP even offered to let Cybercab get first call on battery cells. “We’ll wait our turn,” the firm wrote.

UP founder Ben Schaffer made it clear that he supports Tesla’s all-in move to autonomy, but he wants to keep the Cybertruck program alive.

In a recent development, and it isn’t stopping at the pickup. UP notes it would build the Cybertruck, a three-row “CyberSUV,” and an unmanned “CyberCargo” hauler. Two vehicles Tesla has sometimes referenced, but they were never unveiled.

Sources indicate that the post passed 240,000 views within hours, and the replies are mostly Cybertruck owners and Tesla shareholders begging Musk to say yes. Neither Musk nor Tesla had publicly responded at the time of writing.

UP has a lot riding on this. It sells an entire Cybertruck product line, the UP Invincible lift and armor kits, and it has scored several contracts to turn Cybertrucks into police vehicles for law enforcement agencies. CEO Ben Schaffer once described the organization’s purpose as doing “the things that Tesla maybe wants to do, but doesn’t have the bandwidth to do.” This is that idea taken to its extreme.

Recent findings suggest that musk framed the Cybertruck’s end as a space problem. He said Tesla needs to “make room for increased Cybercab production.”.

If the Cybertruck program was successful, Tesla wouldn’t be killing it. Tesla also produces Model Ys at Giga Texas, and it is not shutting that down to make room for Cybercab.

As we reported when Tesla declared the wind-down, that explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of floor space, the Cybertruck line runs at about a quarter of its 125,000-unit installed capacity, and Texas had only a few hundred Cybercabs registered as of late October.

It has been revealed that the real problem is buyers. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3, and we estimated 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks, a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. That was a good quarter by Cybertruck standards.

Even that number flatters it. S&P Global Mobility data showed SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, about 18% of US registrations that quarter. Tesla also tried a cheaper RWD trim, killed it, released a $60,000 AWD version, then raised prices by $5,000 in August. None of it fixed demand.

I’ll give UP credit for this: the offer calls Musk’s bluff. If the Cybertruck is really dying because Cybercab needs the room, here’s someone volunteering to take the line off Tesla’s plate. Problem solved.

Of course, it’s more complicated than that.

There are many ways this could fail or never happen in the first place, but there’s also a slight possibility that makes this possible.

Recent findings suggest that first off, the backlash is real. If you look on social media and forums, yes, most of the discussion is about how Cybertruck is a failure, and Elon is lying about why Tesla is killing it, but there’s also a serious group of people, especially Cybertruck owners, who are genuinely upset that Tesla is killing the program because they love their trucks.

Most people have never driven a Cybertruck, but the steer-by-wire makes it a very addictive vehicle to drive, and even though the price is high, the value proposition for the specs is not bad compared to the very limited options for electric pickup trucks.

In other words, I wouldn’t necessarily bet against this effort, especially if they add an SUV variant and show the program some love with some tweaks here and there.

It has been revealed that I could see a group of wealthy Cybertruck fans pooling money under Unplugged to make this happen, but getting Tesla to agree could be hard. It’s not unheard of for an automaker to sell a vehicle program to a dealer, like the Lotus Seven and Studebaker Avanti, but it would be a first at this scale.

Industry observers note that who is singing up to light their cash on fire? There is just no way that would work. Unless Tesla just gave them the designs and tooling. Then they are stuck the same problem with who is their market. There are 3 ev trucks coming that are cheaper better and more practical. Likey 3 or 4 more by the end of the decade.

You could make sense of it by looking at UP to Tesla as AMG to Mercedes. It’s not too major a stretch, considering UP isn’t just your average Tesla tuner. It even worked with the automaker on its own version of the Model S Plaid.

If UP were to become for Tesla what AMG has become for Mercedes, it could make some sense for the company to run a separate vehicle program that started under Tesla, but even as I write this, I realize that there’s very little chance this will happen.

But I wish them the best of luck, and I would be happy to see the Cybertruck live on.

Sources indicate that so, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Industry observers note that so, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.
